---
title: "Data"
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("R/_site_helpers.R")
```

Eleven jurisdictions — ten provinces and Canada — observed annually from 1997 to 2019.
**253 complete observations, no missing values.**

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Coverage of the analysis panel."
read_csv("data/processed/panel.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(in_study) |>
  summarise(jurisdictions = n_distinct(geo),
            years = n_distinct(year),
            `first year` = min(year), `last year` = max(year),
            observations = n(),
            `missing values` = sum(if_any(c(gdp_real_2012, ghg_kt, energy_tj), is.na)))
```

## Sources

| Variable | Unit | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Real GDP, chained 2012 dollars | millions | Statistics Canada table [36-10-0402-01](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/cv.action?pid=3610040201) |
| Industrial energy use, final demand | terajoules | Statistics Canada table [25-10-0029-01](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/cv.action?pid=2510002901) |
| Greenhouse gas emissions | kilotonnes CO₂e | [Canada's Official Greenhouse Gas Inventory](https://data.ec.gc.ca/data/substances/monitor/canada-s-official-greenhouse-gas-inventory/A-IPCC-Sector/?lang=en), Environment and Climate Change Canada |

Industry coverage follows the NAICS classification, total of all industries. Statistics
Canada material is used under the [Statistics Canada Open
Licence](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/reference/licence), ECCC material under the [Open
Government Licence – Canada](https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Two things worth knowing about the national series

**Canada is the sum of its parts.** Both GDP and emissions for "Canada" were obtained by
adding the jurisdictions together rather than taken from a separately published national
series — the panel confirms it to rounding. For a study about aggregation, the national
series is therefore an accounting identity over the provincial ones, not an independent
measurement.

**The territories are excluded.** Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut are
carried in the dataset but not analysed: Nunavut and the NWT have essentially no emissions
coverage in this vintage.
:::

## The series

```{r}
#| label: fig-series
#| fig-cap: "All three series, indexed to 1997 = 100. Alberta and Saskatchewan in orange, Ontario in blue."
read_csv("data/processed/panel.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(in_study, geo != "Canada") |>
  pivot_longer(c(gdp_real_2012, ghg_kt, energy_tj),
               names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(series = recode(series, gdp_real_2012 = "real GDP",
                         ghg_kt = "emissions", energy_tj = "energy use")) |>
  group_by(geo, series) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(index = 100 * value / first(value)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(grp = highlight(geo)) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, index, group = geo, colour = grp)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = "grey85") +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = grp != "other"), alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = PALETTE) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.4, `TRUE` = 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ series) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "1997 = 100") +
  theme_site() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92"))
```

## Reproducing this

```bash
git clone <repository>
cd ghg-energy-growth-canada
Rscript -e 'renv::restore()'
Rscript run_all.R
```

The pipeline takes a few seconds. `results/` is committed, so `git diff` after a run
shows whether anything has changed.
